findings.title: SQL injection through concatenation in the invoice search

evidence.fragment: sql = "SELECT id, number, issue_date, total FROM invoices WHERE owner_id = "

findings.explanation: The search parameter 'q' and the owner_id are concatenated straight into the SQL query without parameters, allowing unauthorized data exfiltration.
findings.verification_method: Inject ' OR 1=1 -- into the search query parameter; the response returns other customers' invoices.

findings.title: Monolithic route function with mixed responsibilities
findings.explanation: The 'invoice_new' function has 155 lines and mixes form validation, discount business rules, DB transactions and direct HTML rendering.
findings.verification_method: AST inspection and cyclomatic complexity measured with Radon (CC > 18).

findings.title: Duplicated discount rule with diverging rounding
findings.explanation: Billing rounds the discount on the overall subtotal, while the reports module rounds line by line and then adds up, causing accounting discrepancies.
findings.verification_method: Invoice FY-00001 has a billed discount of 7.51 but shows as 7.50 in the accounting report.

findings.title: Fictitious secret keys written in the source code
findings.explanation: Cryptographic constants and payment gateway credentials declared in plain text in the repository.
findings.verification_method: Static inspection of config.py and a Bandit scan.

findings.title: Deferred circular dependency between business modules
findings.explanation: billing.py imports customers at module level, and customers.py imports billing lazily inside a function, which signals high coupling.
findings.verification_method: Inspection of the import graph and a lazy-loading test.

findings.title: Invoice JSON access without owner authorization (BOLA/IDOR)
findings.explanation: The GET /invoices/<id> endpoint checks that an active session exists but does not validate that the requested invoice belongs to the authenticated user.
findings.verification_method: Log in as user 'bruno' and request invoice 1 of 'ana'; the system answers HTTP 200 with someone else's data.

findings.title: Customer search SQL query correctly parameterized

evidence.fragment: SELECT id, owner_id, name, email FROM customers WHERE email = ?

findings.explanation: Negative control: the query uses SQLite's '?' placeholder. It is not a vulnerability and must stay protected.
findings.verification_method: Characterization test passing synthetic SQL payloads; the query returns zero rows without a syntax error.

architecture_options.name: Progressive extraction with Strangler Fig (Recommended)
pros: Low operational risk: the old and the new system coexist.
First cut verifiable with golden-master characterization tests.
Incremental deployment per endpoint without interrupting the business.
cons: Requires keeping a facade routing layer during the transition.

architecture_options.name: Extraction by leaf modules (Leaf Services)
pros: Decouples components with no incoming dependencies (e.g. reports.py).
Easy to isolate and test in independent containers.
cons: Low direct impact on the value the end user perceives.
Does not fix the critical authentication and BOLA vulnerabilities in the core.

architecture_options.name: Full rewrite from scratch (Big Bang)
pros: 100% new code without dragging legacy decisions along.
cons: Extreme risk of schedule and budget overruns.
Loss of tacit business rules and undocumented edge cases.
Zero value delivered until the end of the project.

pert_plan.name: Phase 1: Pin the contracts and write characterization tests
pert_plan.description: Create a golden-master pytest suite that pins the current observable behavior of GET /invoices/{id}.
assumptions: Access to a test database with known FacturaYa fixtures.
prerequisites: Frozen definition of the v1 JSON contracts.
pert_plan.rollback_strategy: Discard the test suite with no impact on production.

pert_plan.name: Phase 2: FastAPI micro-endpoint and facade router
pert_plan.description: Build the new module in modern/invoices_api.py with Pydantic validation and a facade that routes GET /invoices/{id}.
assumptions: FastAPI can share access to the SQLite database in WAL mode.
prerequisites: Phase 1 approved with 100% of the tests green against the legacy code.
pert_plan.rollback_strategy: Flip the routing flag in the facade back to the original Flask route.

pert_plan.name: Phase 3: Modernize the billing and customers core
pert_plan.description: Rewrite app.invoice_new and billing.py, removing circular dependencies and parameterizing every query.
assumptions: Unit and integration tests cover the rounding calculations.
pert_plan.rollback_strategy: Keep the Flask backend container as an active fallback.

migration_summary.diff_patch:
--- a/samples/facturaya-v1/app.py
+++ b/samples/facturaya-v1/modern/facade.py
@@ -93,14 +93,12 @@
-def invoice_json(invoice_id):
-    # Legacy route vulnerable to BOLA
-    inv = get_invoice(invoice_id)
-    return jsonify(inv)
+from modern.invoices_api import get_invoice_modern
+
+@app.route("/invoices/<int:invoice_id>")
+def invoice_json(invoice_id):
+    # Strangler Fig routing: intercepted and forwarded to modern FastAPI handler
+    return get_invoice_modern(invoice_id, current_user=session.get("user_id"))

details: 100% of the citations point to valid files and line ranges in samples/facturaya-v1/.

executive_summary: CodeArchaeologist completed the forensic diagnosis of FacturaYa v1. It identified 6 real problems (2 critical security issues: SQLi and BOLA/IDOR, 1 fictitious secret, 1 diverging accounting calculation and 1 circular dependency). It recommends a progressive Strangler Fig modernization starting with GET /invoices/{id}, achieving a first step tested green with zero downtime.
